sections.html:
The bill passes through two desks. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) puts a value on the parcel. The Sheriff is where the check goes. McCreary County has no incorporated city, so nobody in the county pays a city levy or visits a city tax window. County government is the only local government covering every resident, and school and district levies fill out the rest of the bill.

Write to the PVA at PO Box 609, Whitley City, KY 42653, phone (606) 376-2514, fax (606) 376-4152. The Sheriff is at (606) 376-2322. The County Clerk, who files deeds and takes over any unpaid bill, is at (606) 376-2411. The fiscal court meets at 1 North Main Street in Whitley City on the second Thursday evening of the month, starting at six.

Under KRS 134.015, value is fixed on January 1 and the bill is meant to be settled before the calendar year closes. The Sheriff will still accept money until April 15, but each step later costs more.

What a McCreary County bill costs by payment date
When you payWhat changes
By November 12 percent discount
November 2 to December 31Face amount on the bill
January5 percent added
After January10 percent added

Miss April 15 and the account goes to the County Clerk. The county attorney mails two warnings, and the tax certificate can be put up for sale three to four and a half months after that handoff. A buyer of the certificate can tack on fees, so square things with the Sheriff first.

sections.h2: What a McCreary County house costs in tax
sections.html:
Bills here are low by Kentucky standards because home values are low. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $85,300. Frankfort's 2025 rate is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value, and the fiscal court, school board and special districts each layer on a levy of their own. Ask the PVA to total them for a specific address.

Owners live in about 74.2 percent of homes. A typical rent runs $577 a month. New construction was nil in 2025, with 0 permits, so the market is almost entirely existing houses. The population was 17,124 in 2025, and the 2020 count showed 6,892 housing units, with about one in eight vacant.

The statewide homestead deduction reaches McCreary County owners too. Turn 65, or be classed as totally disabled, and $49,100 comes off the assessed value for tax years 2025 and 2026 before any rate touches it. On a house near the $85,300 median, that removes a large share of the taxable value.

File in person at the Whitley City PVA office with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport showing your age. A disability claim rests on a government or retirement-plan finding and must be filed again each year. The yearly renewal is waived for owners with a service-connected disability rating and for anyone Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems has found permanently and totally disabled.

Sit down with the PVA or a deputy first. Appeals from owners who skipped that meeting get turned away, and the staff are required to show how your figure was reached. Then:

  • Inspect the roll during the 13 days that follow the first Monday in May.
  • Deliver the written appeal to the County Clerk on or before the first business day after the roll closes.
  • Attach evidence about land and buildings: insurance records, construction costs, comparable sales and photographs. A survey helps with rural tracts. Appeals with no support tend to fail.
  • Go to the hearing of the local board of property owners, held about a month after the roll closes. Evidence is taken only with both sides in the room.

No-shows give up the next stage, the Kentucky Claims Commission. When bills are already printed and the board lands above your claimed value, a supplemental bill collects the gap.

A tax debt follows the house to closing. From January 1 the law treats it as the owner's personal obligation, and a KRS 134.420 lien can hang on for 11 years under any owner. When the account reaches the Clerk, 1 percent interest accrues monthly, and the Clerk and county attorney add commissions along with a recording fee.

Closing agents want a payoff number before funds move. The Sheriff quotes it up to April 15, then the Clerk. Order it early, since the sale price must cover it before the seller nets anything.

For an heir or an owner who has fallen behind, a cash sale as-is skips repair bills and showings and lets you pick a closing date around the payoff. The tax comes out of the proceeds in every case.

sections.h2: Selling a house in McCreary County
sections.html:
McCreary is Kentucky's newest county, carved in 1912 out of Pulaski, Wayne and Whitley, and no incorporated city sits within it. Whitley City is the seat, with Pine Knot and Stearns as the other named communities. Federal land takes up much of the map. The Daniel Boone National Forest covers roughly 43 percent and the Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area roughly 18 percent, so private land is limited.

Population peaked at 18,306 in 2010 and fell 7.7 percent to 16,888 by 2020, then rose 1.4 percent to the 2025 figure. Residents 65 and older make up 17.9 percent of the population, which matters for homestead claims. Prices sit near the county's low median home value, so price carefully and expect buyers to compare against nearby rentals.

sections.h2: What to bring to the office
sections.html: Keep a small folder ready before you call or drive to Whitley City. For the PVA, that means a photo ID, proof of age for a homestead claim, and a copy of your deed. For the Sheriff, bring the parcel number or your last bill so staff can find the account quickly. For the County Clerk, bring any lien notice you have received. Phone ahead, since each office keeps its own hours, and ask what forms of payment the Sheriff takes before you go.

Sales here follow a set order. Get the payoff from the Sheriff or Clerk. Ask the PVA whether a homestead claim sits on the parcel, because dropping it changes the next bill. Collect the deed and any lien papers, and give the payoff to the closing agent so tax is cleared from proceeds. The County Clerk files the new deed after closing.

A house that came through an estate usually needs extra deed work, so bring papers proving who may sell.

Before listing, compare the PVA's record with what you intend to sell: acreage, building description and owner name. A wrong acreage figure is easy to correct with PVA staff, and much harder once a buyer's lender notices it. Rural tracts are where mismatches turn up most, and a recent survey usually settles the question.

faqs.q: Is there a city property tax in McCreary County?
faqs.a: No, since no incorporated city exists here. The bill still carries school and district levies.

faqs.q: Who do I pay for McCreary County property tax?
faqs.a: Send it to the Sheriff, (606) 376-2322, up to April 15. The PVA, (606) 376-2514, handles values and exemption forms, never payments.

faqs.q: What is the state rate for 2025?
faqs.a: It is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value. Local levies are added by the county, school board and districts.

faqs.q: Can a 65-year-old lower the taxable value?
faqs.a: Yes. Show proof of age at the Whitley City PVA office and the homestead deduction removes $49,100 for 2025 and 2026.

faqs.q: What happens if my bill moves to the County Clerk?
faqs.a: The Clerk records a lien and 1 percent monthly interest starts. An investor may buy the certificate three to four and a half months later.
